name: Padella
orderNotes: Fresh handmade pasta, incredible pappardelle and pici cacio e pepe. Best carb-load in London. No reservations — queue only.
reservationHack: No reservations. Join the queue by 17:00 Saturday to avoid 90-min waits.

name: Flat Iron (London Bridge)
orderNotes: Excellent steak and sides. Good for a post-race protein hit. Flat Iron steak with unlimited salad. Free ice cream.
reservationHack: Walk-in only. Arrive early on Saturday evening.

name: Borough Market
orderNotes: London's premier food market. Endless options: pastries, coffee, cooked breakfasts, pasta, cheese, bread. Perfect for spectator fuel or post-race grazing.
reservationHack: No reservation — open market. Arrive early Saturday for best selection.

name: The Ivy Tower Bridge
orderNotes: Brasserie dining near Tower Bridge. Good for a celebratory post-race meal. British classics, cocktails.
reservationHack: Book ahead for Sunday lunch marathon weekend.

name: E Pellicci
orderNotes: Legendary East End Italian cafe since 1900. Full English breakfast, Italian dishes. Grade II listed Art Deco interior. Cash preferred.
reservationHack: No reservations. Opens early — arrive before 08:00 on race Saturday.

name: Dishoom (Tower Bridge)
orderNotes: Bombay-style cafe. Famous for bacon naan rolls at breakfast. Biryani and dal for carb-loading. Beautiful interiors.
reservationHack: Book breakfast online — very popular. Walk-in queue for lunch/dinner.

name: The Mudlark (Greenwich)
orderNotes: Riverside pub right at the start area. Views of Cutty Sark. Classic pub food, good beer selection. Perfect spectator base.
reservationHack: No reservation needed. Arrive early on race morning.

name: Goddards at Greenwich
orderNotes: Traditional pie and mash since 1890. Post-race comfort food. Beef pie, mash, and liquor (parsley sauce). A Greenwich institution.
reservationHack: Counter service, no reservation. Quick turnover.

name: Roka (Canary Wharf)
orderNotes: Contemporary Japanese robata grill. Excellent for a special post-race celebration. Sushi, tempura, grilled meats.
reservationHack: Reserve ahead for Sunday. Call or book online.

name: Wagamama (Various)
orderNotes: Reliable Asian noodle chain. Good carb-loading with ramen and rice dishes. Locations near course at London Bridge, Canary Wharf, Tower Hill.
reservationHack: Walk-in usually fine. Multiple locations provide fallback.

name: Tas Restaurant (London Bridge)
orderNotes: Turkish restaurant with excellent meze and grilled meats. Good portions for carb-loading. Reasonable prices near Borough Market.
reservationHack: Reserve for Saturday dinner on marathon weekend.

name: Franco Manca (Various)
orderNotes: Sourdough pizza chain. Locations at Borough, Canary Wharf, Greenwich. Excellent value Neapolitan-style pizza for carb-loading.
reservationHack: Walk-in usually fine. Arrive before 18:00 Saturday.

name: The Breakfast Club (London Bridge)
orderNotes: All-day breakfast cafe. Pancakes, full English, burritos. Great spectator fuel before heading to viewing spots.
reservationHack: No reservations. Queue early on race Sunday.

name: The Old Brewery (Greenwich)
orderNotes: Cafe-restaurant in the Old Royal Naval College, right at the marathon start area. Breakfast, brunch, and craft beer. Beautiful historic setting.
reservationHack: Book ahead for race weekend. Very close to start line.

name: Pizza Pilgrims (Various)
orderNotes: Wood-fired Neapolitan pizza. Locations near course. Excellent margherita for carb-loading. Fun, casual atmosphere.
reservationHack: Walk-in mostly. Some locations take bookings.

name: The Anchor Bankside
orderNotes: Historic Thames-side pub near Shakespeare's Globe. River views, real ales, traditional pub food. Near mile 24.
reservationHack: No reservation needed for pub area. Book restaurant section.

name: Cafe Murano (Bermondsey)
orderNotes: Angela Hartnett's Italian. Excellent pasta and risotto. Upscale but not stuffy. Perfect for a special Saturday night carb-load.
reservationHack: Reserve well ahead for Saturday dinner marathon weekend.

name: Pret A Manger (Various)
orderNotes: Ubiquitous London chain. Reliable early-morning breakfast option when nothing else is open. Porridge, croissants, coffee. Multiple locations along course.
reservationHack: No reservation. Just walk in.

name: The Rake (Borough)
orderNotes: Tiny craft beer pub next to Borough Market. Excellent rotating craft beer selection. Standing room mostly. Good for a quick post-race pint.
reservationHack: No reservation — tiny pub. Arrive early.

name: Bao (London Bridge)
orderNotes: Taiwanese steamed buns and small plates. Light, flavorful post-race option. Classic milk bao is unmissable.
reservationHack: Queue only — no reservations. Popular spot.

name: Victoria Station Food Court
orderNotes: Multiple options in the station. Reliable fallback for any meal. Also serves as proven reunion point near the finish area.
reservationHack: No reservation needed.

name: The Gun (Canary Wharf)
orderNotes: Georgian docklands pub with Thames views. Excellent Sunday roast. Near the Canary Wharf section of the course (mile 17-19).
reservationHack: Book for Sunday lunch on marathon weekend.

name: Leon (Various)
orderNotes: Healthy fast food chain. Good for quick post-race recovery meals. Chicken, rice bowls, salads. Multiple locations along course.
reservationHack: Counter service, no reservation.

name: Cecconi's (City of London)
orderNotes: Upscale Italian at The Ned hotel. Handmade pasta, wood-fired pizza, excellent wine list. Beautiful Art Deco setting.
reservationHack: Reserve well ahead for Saturday dinner.

name: Nandos (Various)
orderNotes: Peri-peri chicken chain. Reliable carb-load with rice/chips sides. Multiple locations. Familiar and affordable.
reservationHack: Walk-in. Most locations have space.

name: Hawksmoor (Borough)
orderNotes: Premier steakhouse. Excellent for a celebratory post-race dinner. British beef, great cocktails. Borough location near the course.
reservationHack: Reserve well ahead. Very popular.

name: Monmouth Coffee (Borough)
orderNotes: Legendary London coffee roaster. Small cafe at Borough Market. Excellent espresso and filter coffee. Limited food but perfect pre-race caffeine.
reservationHack: No reservation. Queue may be long — arrive early.

name: Iberica (Canary Wharf)
orderNotes: Spanish restaurant with excellent tapas and paella. Good carb-loading alternative to Italian. Terrace with Docklands views.
reservationHack: Book for Saturday dinner on marathon weekend.

name: The Trafalgar St James
orderNotes: Hotel bar/restaurant overlooking Trafalgar Square, short walk from The Mall finish. Rooftop bar with views. Good for a celebration drink.
reservationHack: Book ahead for marathon Sunday.

name: Ye Olde Cheshire Cheese
orderNotes: Historic pub rebuilt in 1667 after the Great Fire. Atmospheric vaulted cellars. Traditional pub food and real ales. Near mile 24 of the course.
reservationHack: Walk-in. Can get crowded but has multiple floors.
hoursProofText: Mon-Sat 11:00-23:00. Closed Sunday — check race day hours.
